deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the opening of the main text of Riemann's 1857 fragment 'Zwei allgemeine Theoreme über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten', printed in his Werke (1876) from the Nachlass. The previous page is the introduction and the definitions of 'einändrig' and 'Verzweigungswerth'.

(1) Setting. Let y = (y_1,...,y_n) be functions of x. They are single-valued (einändrig) and finite for all complex x except finitely many branch values a, b, c, ..., g. A positive circuit of x around any one branch value takes the y's into linear combinations of their former values with constant coefficients.

(2) Cut plane. The x-plane is cut by a closed line running through all branch values in the order a, b, ..., g. In each part of the plane so obtained the y's are single-valued. The values on the positive side of the line are taken as given.

(3) Local monodromy. A positive circuit around a sends y_ν to Σ_ι A^ν_ι y_ι. A positive circuit around b sends y_ν to Σ_ι B^ν_ι y_ι, and so on for the other branch values. Notation: (A) is the n×n matrix (A^ν_ι), likewise (B), ..., (G). (y) is the column of values. (A)(y) is the column of the Σ_ι A^ν_ι y_ι.

(4) Global relation. The claim is (G)(F)...(B)(A) = identity. Riemann writes the right side as (0) and defines it as the substitution leaving the values unchanged: off-diagonal entries 0, diagonal entries 1.
- Proof: move x along the positive side of the cut from one branch value to the next. Then (y) becomes successively (A)(y), (B)(A)(y), ..., (G)(F)...(B)(A)(y).
- That path is equivalent to traversing the negative side of the cut, i.e. the whole boundary of the other region.
- The y's are single-valued in that region, so they must return to their original values. Hence the product is the identity.
- [Mine] This tacitly assumes the second region contains no branch point, so ∞ is either regular or counted among a,...,g.
- In modern terms: the product of the local monodromies around all singular points, taken in the right order, is 1. This is the defining relation of the fundamental group of the sphere minus the points a, ..., g.

(5) The P-symbol. A system with these properties is denoted P( a b c ... g ; A B C ... G ; x ). Riemann then announces that he will study all systems with the same branch values and the same substitutions, i.e. the same monodromy class. He says there are infinitely many.

(6) Diagonalization. Citing a known theorem, a substitution can 'generally speaking' be written as a product of three: A = (α)·diag(λ_1,...,λ_n)·(α)^{-1}. The middle factor only multiplies each quantity by a factor. The λ_i are the roots of an n-th degree equation fully determined by (A); [mine] this is det(A − λI) = 0. The case of equal roots would need a modified middle factor ([mine] Jordan form) and is excluded for now.

(7) What comes next (following page): pass to z = (α)^{-1} y, so that a circuit around a sends z_i to λ_i z_i. Then z_i (x−a)^{−log λ_i/(2πi)} is single-valued near a, which leads to the exponents μ_i and to the extended P-symbol.
errors: Order of composition is a convention issue, not a substantive error. With (A)(y) read literally as the matrix product A·y, continuing Ay around b gives A(By) = AB·y, not BA·y. The relation written (G)...(B)(A) = 1 is therefore correct only if (B)(A) means 'first A, then B' as substitutions acting on the variables. Read as plain matrix products the relation would be A B ... G = 1. The two versions differ by passing to inverses/transposes and define the same group up to isomorphism.
Tacit assumption, not stated: the complementary region bounded by the cut contains no further singularity, so ∞ is either regular or listed among the branch values.

The diagonalization step is valid only for distinct eigenvalues (more precisely, for diagonalizable A). Riemann explicitly excludes the case of equal roots, so this is a stated restriction, not an error.

results.what: Multivalued solution systems on the plane minus finitely many points: an analytic circuit around each branch point acts by a constant linear substitution
results.modern_name: Monodromy representation of a local system / Fuchsian system
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1857 hypergeometric paper and this Nachlass fragment); developed by Fuchs (1866) and later authors

results.what: Product of the local monodromy matrices around all singular points, in cyclic order along a cut, equals the identity
results.modern_name: Monodromy relation M_g···M_a = 1 (fundamental group of the punctured sphere)

results.what: P-symbol for systems with given branch points and given monodromy substitutions; study of all systems in the same class
results.modern_name: Riemann P-symbol generalized to n-th order; setup of the Riemann–Hilbert problem

results.what: Monodromy matrix written as A = α diag(λ_i) α^{-1}, with λ_i the roots of the characteristic equation (distinct roots assumed)
results.modern_name: Diagonalization / eigen-decomposition (Jordan normal form in general)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the beginning of Riemann's well-known 1857 fragment on linear ODEs with algebraic coefficients, published in his Werke (1876) and widely discussed as the origin of the monodromy and Riemann–Hilbert ideas. Its content is already credited to him.

checkable.asserts: A matrix with distinct eigenvalues factors as (alpha)*diag(lambda)*(alpha)^-1
The lambda_i are the roots of the n-th degree characteristic equation determined by A
Rank-1 check of the product relation: (x-a)^mu (x-b)^(1-mu) has local monodromies whose product is 1 (exponent sum is an integer, so infinity is not a branch point)
The composition order in (G)...(B)(A)=1 matters, since monodromy matrices generally do not commute

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the image reads 'eindeutig' (consistent with the previous page's 'einändrig'), and the list of exceptions is a, b, c ... (later up to g), not just 'a, b, c [?]'.
'(0)' on the right side of equation (1) is as written. Riemann defines it as the identity substitution (diagonal 1, off-diagonal 0), so it means the identity, not the zero matrix.
'des negativ unendlich liegenden Gebiets' is doubtful. The sense is 'the region lying on the negative side' (the complementary region); 'unendlich' is probably a misreading.
'die die Reihe der Verzweigungswerthe sämmtlich trifft' should be read as: the line passes through all branch values in order (der Reihe nach).

The cited theorem about decomposing a substitution is introduced as 'nach einem bekannten Satze' (the reading of the following words is uncertain). The decomposition is A=(α)diag(λ)(α)^{-1} with λ_i the roots of an equation n-ten Grades.
